definition: The task of converting written text into natural-sounding spoken audio.
details: Modern text-to-speech systems increasingly use neural network architectures (including diffusion and transformer-based models) to produce highly natural, expressive synthetic speech.

explainer.lead: The task of turning written text into natural-sounding speech. It matters because it makes written content usable by voice interfaces and by people who cannot read the screen.

tiers.eli5: You give the computer some writing, and it says it out loud in a voice that sounds natural.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers increasingly build on neural architectures, including diffusion and transformer-based models, to get expressive, natural output. Pitfall: expressiveness must still match the intended content, since highly natural speech in the wrong tone misleads listeners.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as converting written text into natural-sounding spoken audio. Modern systems increasingly use neural network architectures, including diffusion and transformer-based models, for highly natural, expressive speech.

explainer.example: A phone app reads an incoming message aloud using a transformer-based model that produces an expressive, human-like voice.
